Every plant now has its own attack cue (y62) and every pest death fades (3t9); the projectile connecting them has no impact flash, spark, or differently-timed vanish to say a hit landed. Add a brief impact cue (a small flash/particle burst or a one-frame flicker on the pest hit) distinct from a kernel simply leaving the board.
close_reason: Kernel connects now flash the surviving pest (Pest.flash_hit / hit_flash_color), gated by GardenTheme.animations_enabled(); a lethal hit still relies on the existing corpse/fade/PEST_KILLED cue. Verified headless (name_check, import, lint, run_tests 420/420) and live via devtools bridge (step-time caught modulate mid-flash at 1.43, boosted above 1.0).

title: None of the three attacking plants calls Sfx.play() for its own attack
description: CornCobbler._fire_at() (corn_cobbler.gd:116-132) spawns kernels and calls _recoil() with no sound; ChompFlower._grab()/_bite() (chomp_flower.gd:77-84,139-144) closes the mouth with no sound; StickySundew._claim() (sticky_sundew.gd:244-250) has the same gap. Every combat sound today is centralised in game.gd and fires on the pest's reaction (Sfx.PEST_KILLED, Sfx.PLANT_BITTEN) rather than the attacker's own action, so a Corn Cobbler volleying five kernels or a Chomp snapping shut are silent on the attacker's end. Add a distinct Sfx entry per plant's own attack verb, played from the plant itself at the moment it acts.
close_reason: Added CORN_FIRED, CHOMP_BITE, SUNDEW_CLAIM to Sfx, each reusing an existing vendored stream; wired into CornCobbler._fire_at, ChompFlower._bite, StickySundew._claim. Commit a2f91d9.

title: Plant idle sway is a dead field
description: Plant._wobble_time (plant.gd:104) is declared and never read or written anywhere else in the file - a sweep of every var declared in game/ found exactly one field with no second reference. Wire it up: a small sin(_wobble_time * k) sway on _sprite.rotation (or similar idle motion), gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), incremented in _physics_process. Ties to James's direct ask ('animate all the plants and enemies') - this is the hook already sitting there for exactly that, unwired. Scope to Plant only for this issue; pests can follow separately.
close_reason: Wired _wobble_time into _physics_process; small sin() sway on the sprite, gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), phased per-cell. Commit 5792e57.

title: Clearing a wave gets a single status-row sentence, starting one gets a banner and a sound
description:
Game._check_wave_cleared() (game.gd:322-338) sets _wave_live = false, commits the
lane pressure map, and calls hud.show_message(Hud.wave_cleared_line(...), 6.0) -- no
Sfx.play(), no flash, nothing on the board itself. _on_wave_started plays
Sfx.WAVE_STARTED (game.gd:272) into a 48px banner the instant a wave begins
(Hud.announce_wave, hud.gd:1044-1053). The wave a player survives currently
announces itself more quietly than the wave about to attack them. Give clearing a
wave its own cue -- a Sfx entry and/or a brief board-level flourish -- proportionate
to what it is.
close_reason: Added Sfx.WAVE_CLEARED and Hud.announce_wave_cleared, sharing the banner mechanism via _show_banner; wired into _check_wave_cleared alongside the existing status line. Commit 075fce9.

title: RunSummary's entrance does not know whether the run was won or lost
description:
_build_heading() (run_summary.gd:144-153) picks a different heading text and colour
for victory ("The garden holds!" vs "The garden is eaten"), but _play_entrance()
(run_summary.gd:462-470) rises every Control by the identical RISE_OFFSET over the
identical RISE_SECONDS with no branch on `won` anywhere in it. Give a win and a loss
distinct entrance motion (or a distinct one-shot flourish, e.g. a brief flash/shake
on loss) so the card's motion agrees with what its heading already says.
close_reason: Entrance branches on won: faster/overshoot rise for a win, slower plain rise for a loss. Commit 9e06db2.

title: A pest corpse pops out of existence instead of fading
description:
_play_death() (pest.gd:484-505) swaps to the dead-eyes texture, holds it for
DEATH_LINGER (0.35s, pest.gd:136), then tween.tween_callback(queue_free) -- nothing
tweens modulate.a first, so the corpse is at full opacity on its last frame and
simply gone the next. Every other exit in this game fades: Plant.play_exit_and_free()
shrinks a sprite to zero before freeing, and a pest's own arrival fades it in. Add a
short fade-out (gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled()) into the existing
tween chain before queue_free.
close_reason: modulate:a now tweens to 0 over the tail of DEATH_LINGER, gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(); commit ab3d8f3

title: Pests never turn to face the direction they're walking
description:
Requested directly by James (kanban.md, 'Requested directly by James' block). Pest
sprites are drawn up-screen per the art style convention, but pest.gd has no
rotation/flip_h/flip_v logic anywhere -- a pest walking down, left, or right the road
still renders facing up-screen the whole way. Give Pest a facing update (rotation or
flip, whichever the kit's sprites tolerate) driven off its walk direction each leg of
PATH_CORNERS.
close_reason: Sprite rotates to face the leg it is walking, snapped to 4 cardinal directions off Board's axis-aligned route; commit 3815587

title: A plant leaving the board always vanishes silently
description: Both Game._on_plant_destroyed (game.gd:987-995) and Game.uproot_selected (game.gd:1084-1093) end in plant.queue_free() with no exit animation; uproot additionally has zero Sfx.play() call anywhere in the function. Neither tweens the sprite out the way Plant._build_visuals tweens one in (plant.gd:187-190, 0.4x to 1.12x to 1.0 over 0.22s). A create_tween() shrinking _sprite.scale toward zero before either queue_free() call, gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), plus an Sfx entry for uproot specifically, would give leaving the board the same care arriving on it gets.
close_reason: Shipped: Plant.play_exit_and_free() tween-out + Sfx.PLANT_UPROOTED, commit 6117da4

title: Corn Cobbler upgrades have no moment of their own
description: CornCobbler.upgrade() (corn_cobbler.gd:290-297) bumps level and calls queue_redraw() -- a static fact the muzzle fan picks up next paint, not a cue at the instant the player spends the seeds. Contrast ChompFlower._bite() (chomp_flower.gd:139-144), which squashes its sprite on every single meal. A short scale-pop on the cob's sprite plus a new Sfx entry, gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), would mark the transaction rather than only its aftermath.
close_reason: Shipped: _upgrade_flourish() squash tween + Sfx.PLANT_UPGRADED, commit 388db1a

title: A refused purchase has a sentence and no other feedback
description: SeedBank.pay_for_plant() and buy_packet() both emit purchase_failed with only a reason string on every refusal (seed_bank.gd:111-121, 179-190), and Game._ready wires it straight to hud.show_message(reason) - a caption in the shared status line, nothing more. Sfx.SOUNDS has entries for planting, a plant dying, a pest dying, a wave starting, but none for a purchase bouncing. Add a denial cue: a short red shake on the button actually clicked (or the plant bar slot) plus a new Sfx.SOUNDS entry, so the 'no' lands where the click happened instead of only in text a player mid-wave may not be reading.
close_reason: Shipped: Sfx.PURCHASE_DENIED (reuses error_002.ogg) plays on every bank.purchase_failed; Hud.shake_plant_button/shake_packet_button shake the specific control at the two call sites that know which one was reached for. Commit 2a162f3.

title: Selecting a plant has no motion
description: Plant.set_selected() (plant.gd:462-468) toggles _selection_marker.visible directly and SelectionMarker._draw_brackets() (selection_marker.gd:41-46) draws the four corner brackets at fixed size the instant the flag flips - no tween, nothing between invisible and full-size. Contrast _build_visuals(), which pops a placed plant's sprite in from 0.4x scale over 0.22s (plant.gd:187-190). Give the selection brackets (and by inheritance PlacementPreview's hover cue) a short grow-in/fade tween instead of an instant show, gated behind GardenTheme.animations_enabled().
close_reason: Shipped: SelectionMarker.play_entrance() grows brackets in from 0.55x/transparent. PlacementPreview stays instant (hover cue, redraws every mouse move) -- documented in the commit. Commit 506a0f9.

title: HUD readouts snap instead of punching on change
description: Hud.refresh() overwrites _seeds_label.text, _lives_label.text and _compost_label.text outright every call (hud.gd:731,753,755), while the same file already eases the wave label's colour with a killed-and-restarted Tween in _ease_threat_tint (hud.gd:898-911) instead of snapping it. Give the seeds/lives/compost labels a short scale-punch when their value changes, gated the same way _ease_threat_tint already is (GardenTheme.animations_enabled()), so the game's three most frequent feedback moments (a kill payout, a life lost, a husk composted) get the one motion vocabulary this file has already proven out.
close_reason: Shipped: seeds/lives/compost labels get a scale punch on change, reusing _ease_threat_tint's kill-and-restart Tween pattern. Commit 7296b78.

title: PauseScreen has no entrance or exit motion
description: PauseScreen's own header calls it shaped after RunSummary, being the same kind of object: a card over a live board (pause_screen.gd:12-14). RunSummary and TitleScreen both rise their content in against GardenTheme.animations_enabled(); PauseScreen has no create_tween or modulate write anywhere in the file. The card appears via add_child and disappears via _pause_layer.queue_free() (game.gd:821) on the same frame Escape is pressed. Add a rise-in / fade-out matching the other two card screens' pattern, gated the same way.
close_reason: Shipped: rise-in entrance borrowing RunSummary's constants, and a play_exit() fade Game.resume_run() awaits before freeing the layer. Commit 54152de.

title: Corn Cobbler needs a readiness readout
description: Sunflower's payout clock has an always-on fill gauge (sunflower.gd ~150-156) and Chomp Flower's mouth shows a shrinking chew ring (chomp_flower.gd _draw ~130-136), but CornCobbler._cooldown (corn_cobbler.gd:88, ticked at ~95-97) is read by nothing outside _act(). The muzzle fan (_draw_muzzle_fan, ~141-152) reflects the last shot's spread, not the next shot's timing, so a cob mid-reload and one ready to fire look identical. Add a readiness cue (fill ring, dimming muzzle, or similar) driven off _cooldown / LEVELS interval, matching the visual idiom the other two plants already use.
close_reason: Readiness fade shipped: readiness_at()/readiness() drive a 0.35-1.0 alpha fade on the muzzle fan, off the same _cooldown _act already ticks. Unit-tested exactly (pure math + wired through real _act()); live-confirmed via forced fires (0.02-0.10 readiness right after firing, 1.0 once recovered), zero runtime errors across 7 placed cobblers. Baseline regenerated (fire_interval() is now genuinely test-named). Commit follows.

title: Find tests that read state straight after instantiate_scene
description: test_hosting_a_loaded_cob asserted a volley had fired by the time instantiate_scene returned. That frame count is unspecified, so it was order-dependent - green two cycles, red when unrelated tests shifted timing. Any test reading a group or a live property straight after instantiate_scene without awaiting a condition has the same exposure. A checker for that shape would name them.
close_reason: Closed

title: Tell the player unaimed ground still gets kills
description: Coverage is now measured both directions and neither number is in the game. Under-promise: 7 kills on unaimed ground at up to 202px, because a kernel flies until it leaves the board. Over-promise at the pest: zero of 116. The board says 'unaimed', which is right, but a player never learns unaimed ground still gets kills - which is what would stop them over-buying cover.
close_reason: Closed

title: Assert what Pest.died and escaped carry
description: 15 signals still have nothing asserting what they carry, down from 17. Pest.died is the highest value remaining: it is the income path with the most wiring under it (Game._on_pest_died drops the husk, banks seeds, notes the lane loss). escaped is its pair. Assert the payload and which paths fire, not merely that the signal exists - naming it satisfies the reach gate while proving nothing.
close_reason: Closed

title: No gate says how much of the game the suite never touches
description: run_tests prints Suite: 7 scripts and Assertions: N; the checkers print N of M; lint prints Shaders: N of M. Nothing prints which .gd files are never loaded by any test. The bridge already has scripts-seen and nothing compares it against the file list. That is the one denominator the project lacks, and it is the one that says where the suite is blind.
close_reason: Closed

title: Tell the player which red means fought and which means unreachable
description: coverage_frontier() says how far the garden can reach; LanePressureOverlay says how far pests got. The prep line compares them once to pick a sentence. The board never does - a player sees red tint and cannot tell 'they got here and we fought' from 'they got here and nothing could touch them', which is the whole distinction the coverage work established.
close_reason: Closed

title: Warn at startup when a budget crosses its own tight threshold
description: cmd budgets reports tight/spent from outside, but nothing inside the game reacts. A startup push_warning when any budget crosses its tight threshold means the next person to spend one hears about it on the next run rather than on the next audit. Reuses the budget entries the verb already computes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Tests leak nodes into groups and nothing notices
description: Root cause under the kernels flake: a test that builds a Kernel and does not free it leaves it in the group for every later test. _T.free_ui is called on hosts, but a kernel spawned by _act is parented to the host's PARENT, not the host. A per-test assertion that group counts return to where they started would catch the whole class.
close_reason: Closed

title: Two HUD budgets sit within 8px of their ceilings
description: cmd budgets reports hud_readouts at 161 of 168px (SeedsLabel, 7px left) and hud_stats_row at 1104 of 1112px (8px left). Both are 'tight' by the verb's own <15% threshold. The row sum is the one that matters: widening any single readout is paid out of it, so the two are coupled and both are nearly gone. Worth deciding now whether the stats row needs re-proportioning before the next readout is added rather than after.
close_reason: Shipped: trimmed STATS_SEPARATION 14->10, flat +10px readout margins, ratcheted BUDGET_FLOOR, commit e93241c

title: SIMULTANEOUS_PEST_CEILING is fully spent and nothing said so
description: cmd budgets reports pest_road_ceiling at 40 of 40 pests, 0 left, state 'spent'. That is by construction - the ceiling is enforced by the group shares summing to it exactly - but it means the road budget has no slack at all, so any future wave shape that wants more simultaneous pests has nowhere to take them from. Decide whether 'spent by design' deserves its own state distinct from 'spent because you ran out'.
close_reason: Shipped: Game.BUDGET_SPENT_BY_DESIGN state, pest_road_ceiling passes by_design=true, commit 34a77ae

title: The post-mortem names a cell the road under it may not be reddest at
description: stop_cell is losses-minus-escapes; the tint under the translucent summary card is still painted from raw losses. On a bleeding run the named cell and the reddest cell genuinely differ. Correct and documented, but a player looking from the number to the picture is told nothing. Either the card points at its own cell, or the tint switches to stops.
close_reason: Closed

title: A budgets verb that prints every declared coupling with its headroom
description: Four constants now carry 'moving me costs you X' comments: PATH_CORNERS, COLLECT_RADIUS, SUBHEAD_MAX_WIDTH and the HUD WORST_CASE_TEXT budgets. Each warns about a coupling living in another file, and a person only finds the warning by editing that exact line. A devtools verb printing every declared budget with its current headroom makes the set visible before someone goes looking.
close_reason: Closed

title: Name the husk budget where the road is actually edited
description: board_info now reports the husk click budget, but reaching it needs a running game, a launched bridge and knowing the verb exists. A designer dragging Board.PATH_CORNERS is in board.gd in an editor and nothing there mentions the budget. Add a ## line above PATH_CORNERS and above CompostMeter.COLLECT_RADIUS naming it. Suggested by the agent that built the devtools half, which correctly judged its own work a half-solution.
close_reason: Closed

title: Give the board a second warning channel so red is not carrying three meanings
description: GardenTheme.DANGER now paints lane pressure (pests got this far), the plant health bar (this plant is dying) and an armed Uproot (you are about to destroy this). Three different sentences in one hue at three alphas. Unifying the value was right; colour alone should not carry three meanings - add a shape or hatch channel.
close_reason: Closed

title: Put husk_click_margin in board_info so the budget is visible before a test fails
description: husk_click_margin() exists because the husk-vs-placement conflict is 4px from being real, and a test asserts the clearance stays positive. Nothing tells a designer moving PATH_CORNERS or COLLECT_RADIUS that they are spending it - they find out when a test fails, with no indication 4px was the budget.
close_reason: Closed

title: Show lane pressure during prep, not after the run
description: LanePressureOverlay paints how far pests got, decayed once per wave, and is a readout of the wave that just ended. Board.run_pressure_alpha exists and is shown exactly once by show_run_pressure(), at the moment the run is over. The number that would inform a purchase is held back until purchasing has stopped. Surface it during the prep strip.
close_reason: Closed

title: The notebook is unreachable the moment a run starts
description: NotebookScreen is constructed in exactly one place, title_screen.gd's _open_notebook(), and nothing in game.gd, hud.gd or pause_screen.gd can reach it. So the game's only explanation of anything is closed to the player who actually needs it -- mid-run, holding a plant they do not understand. The pause card is now a full-screen surface that already lists the keyboard verbs and is already the only way to leave a run; a fourth button on it is the whole fix. NotebookScreen already emits back_requested and is built to be added as a child of any Control.
acceptance_criteria: The notebook opens from within a run and returns to the paused game, with the run still paused behind it. A test asserts the pause state survives opening and closing it.
close_reason: Closed

title: The endless spawn gap floors at wave 22 and only the count keeps climbing
description: WaveDirector's aphid spawn gap reaches its floor around wave 22, and the health and speed scales cap around waves 41 and 48. Past 48 the only thing that still moves is count, which is uncapped -- 166 pests at wave 48, 376 at wave 108. Spawn floor times crossing time puts on the order of 100 aphids alive at once on an 896px board. That is precisely the quantity problem the ENDLESS_HEALTH_STEP header says the scales exist to avoid, arrived at from the other direction.
acceptance_criteria: Endless difficulty past the scale caps escalates by something other than raw count, or count is bounded and the difficulty comes from elsewhere. A test asserts simultaneous pest count stays under a stated ceiling at wave 100.
close_reason: Closed

title: A husk eats the click that would have planted, and the preview cannot warn about it
description: CompostMeter.COLLECT_RADIUS is 28, so a husk claims a 56px-wide target on a 64px cell -- 88% of it. Game._click_at sweeps a husk before it reaches the placement branch and returns, so a click on a cell the preview has just drawn as legal composts instead of planting. PlacementPreview now computes four states (illegal, at_risk, dead ground, redundant coverage) and mentions husks exactly zero times, so the one thing that can silently take the click is the one thing the ring cannot warn about. Husks last up to 10s, so the cell is effectively unplantable for that long with no indication.
acceptance_criteria: Either the preview shows that a click on this cell will compost rather than plant, or placement wins on a cell the player has explicitly targeted. Unit test covers a husk overlapping a buildable cell.
close_reason: Precedence fixed: a click that would plant, plants. Measurement showed the conflict cannot occur on the shipping board (32px vs a 28px sweep, 4px margin) -- husk_click_margin() now gates that

title: Every Sundew redraw walks every pest on the board
description: StickySundew._draw_wash calls shared_ground_offsets, which calls _sibling_patches, which walks all of _entities' children -- and pests live there too. So the cost of drawing one patch scales with the number of pests, not the number of patches. _refresh_droplets queues a redraw whenever droplet_radius changes, which it does as pests enter and leave the patch, so the redraws are most frequent exactly when the pest count is highest. Sundew membership changes at only two sites, so the sibling list could be cached and invalidated there instead.
acceptance_criteria: Drawing a patch does not iterate pests. A test asserts the sibling lookup is not called per-pest, or that redraw cost is independent of pest count.
close_reason: Closed

title: The 45-seed Corn upgrade is worse than the 20-seed one against a single pest
description: CornCobbler.LEVELS with evenly-spaced offsets puts level 3's kernels at +/-26, +/-13 and 0 degrees. Against Kernel.HIT_RADIUS 18.0 an outer kernel clears the aimed pest past 18/tan(26) = 37px -- under one cell, against a RANGE of 176. Level 2's +/-7 degrees connects out to 147px. Single-target that is level 2 at 2.78 dps versus level 3 at 1.61, and damage is 1.0 at all three levels. So the most expensive upgrade in the game makes a cob worse against the thing it is aimed at, while the selection panel advertises '5 kernel(s) per shot' and the muzzle fan draws the spread as the benefit.
acceptance_criteria: Each upgrade level is at least as good as the one below it against a single target, or the spread's cost is stated where the player buys it. A test asserts single-target dps is non-decreasing across levels.
close_reason: Closed

title: The pause note is drawn underneath the first button
description: PauseScreen.FIRST_BUTTON_Y is an absolute 232.0 -- the one offset in that file not written as CARD.position.y + N. With CARD at y=152 the Note's box is 228-252 and ResumeButton's is 232-276, so 20 of the note's 24 pixels sit under an opaque stylebox. There is 64px of unused card below the last button. This is a sibling-pair overlap, the class validate-ui and findings structurally cannot see because each Control fits its own box; the repo ships .claude/skills/godot-hud-occlusion-audit for exactly this. The note text is also a constant, 'The wave is waiting.', which is false whenever pause fires between waves.
acceptance_criteria: No pause-screen Control overlaps another, asserted by a pairwise test, and the note says something true about the current state.
close_reason: Closed

title: Two Sundews on the same ground cost 60 seeds and slow nothing extra
description: StickySundew refcounts its slow so overlapping patches hold a pest at 0.55 rather than 0.30 -- correct, and deliberate. But the patch wash composites darker where two patches overlap, so the only thing on screen says the opposite of the rule: it reads as 'more slow here'. A player can spend 60 seeds on two patches covering the same road and get exactly what one would have given. The placement preview has no notion of ground already covered, and crossing_time_multiplier() has no caller outside a test.
acceptance_criteria: Overlapping Sundew ground is visually distinguishable from stacked-and-working, or the preview warns before the second one is placed. A test covers the overlap case.
close_reason: Closed

title: There is no pause, and no way to leave a run you are done with
description: get_tree().paused appears nowhere in game/. Game._unhandled_input handles motion, left click, KEY_R gated on game over, and KEY_M for mute -- there is no pause key. PREP_SECONDS keeps counting down while the player is away from the keyboard, so stepping away mid-run loses beds. TITLE_SCENE is reachable only from RunSummary's GateButton, which means the only way out of a run in progress is to lose it or kill the process. The devtools bridge answers while the tree is paused, so a pause menu is verifiable.
acceptance_criteria: A pause key freezes the run including the prep timer, and offers a way back to the title screen. Unit test asserts the prep timer does not advance while paused.
close_reason: Closed

title: Nothing in the catalogue answers a hungry pest
description: Sticky Sundew deliberately does not answer is_hungry: a hungry pest stops to eat a plant at EAT_DPS 14.0 against Plant.MAX_HEALTH 40.0, under three seconds per bed, and eating is not movement-gated so a slow does nothing about it. Every plant in the catalogue either damages a pest or funds the ones that do; nothing protects or repairs a bed under attack. A real answer needs a regen or armour hook on Plant, which is why it was filed rather than faked.
acceptance_criteria: A plant, upgrade or mechanic exists that meaningfully changes the outcome when a hungry pest reaches a bed. Unit test drives a hungry pest against a defended and an undefended bed and asserts the difference.
close_reason: Closed

title: A plant's health only goes down, and the cheapest repair is to destroy it
description: Plant.take_damage is the only writer of health and there is no heal path anywhere. uproot_refund reads PlantCatalog.cost * 0.6 and never reads health, so uprooting a nearly-dead plant refunds exactly as much as uprooting a pristine one -- making uproot-and-replant the cheapest repair in the game at a net 4 seeds for a Corn. That is a strictly dominant strategy that also makes the new health readout advisory rather than a decision.
acceptance_criteria: Either damaged plants can be healed at a cost, or the uproot refund scales with remaining health so a wrecked plant refunds less. Unit test covers the refund at full and near-zero health.
close_reason: Closed

title: The placement ring is drawn with equal confidence over cells that cover no road at all
description: PlacementPreview computes reach and legality per cell but legality only means buildable-and-empty. Measured against the real PATH_CORNERS route: of 94 buildable cells, 15 cover zero road at a Corn Cobbler's RANGE of 176px, and 34 cover zero road at a Chomp Flower's GRAB_RADIUS of 73.6px. The ring looks identical on all of them, so a player can spend 10 seeds on a plant that can never fire, and nothing says so before or after the click.
acceptance_criteria: A cell that covers no road for the currently selected plant is visually distinct in the preview before the click. Unit test asserts the covered-road count per cell against the real route for both plants.
close_reason: Closed

title: One high score serves both game modes, and the title screen names it wrong
description: Game._end_run calls RunConfig.record_score with the run's seed total and no mode check, and RunConfig persists a single number to user://highscore.save. TitleScreen renders that one number as 'Best endless run' / 'No endless run on record yet'. So a campaign run can take the endless record, and RunSummary._score_line then compares a campaign total against a number that may have come from an endless run. Two different games are sharing one scoreboard and the label claims otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: Campaign and endless keep separate high scores, each labelled for the mode it came from, and an existing single-value save migrates without being lost. Unit test covers a campaign run not overwriting an endless record.
close_reason: Closed

title: The game makes no sound at all
description: A repo-wide grep for AudioStreamPlayer, AudioStream, .ogg and .wav finds no hit anywhere in game code -- assets/ holds only kenney/ and sprites/. Four new cues shipped in cycle 3-4 (uproot arming, plant damage, threat escalation, mutation markers) and not one of them makes a noise. The silent-death case is the worst: compost_meter erases an expired husk with no cue at all, so the player never learns they were too slow. Kenney ships CC0 audio packs in the same collection the sprites came from.
acceptance_criteria: At least placement, pest death, husk collection, husk rot and run end have distinct sounds, with a master mute honoured (devtools_config.json already sets mute:true for automation). A test asserts every declared sound file exists and loads.
close_reason: 11 CC0 Kenney samples, 8-voice root-parented pool, silent-husk-rot fixed; verified live catching a voice mid-playback and surviving a scene reload

title: A mutated pest is a tint, and the two that change the rules are unnamed
description: Pest mutations are signalled only by a _tint colour. Winged makes a Chomp Flower unable to grab it at all (chomp_flower.gd skips pests with is_winged) and hungry makes it eat a plant at EAT_DPS 14.0 against Plant.MAX_HEALTH 40.0 -- under three seconds to destroy a bed. Both change what the player should do and neither is named or shaped differently. The placement preview already computes at_risk, so the vocabulary for warning about this exists.
acceptance_criteria: A winged and a hungry pest are each distinguishable from a plain one by something other than hue -- a shape, an icon, or a label -- and the distinction survives a screenshot in greyscale.
close_reason: Closed

title: Nothing counts down the 18 seconds to the next wave
description: Game.PREP_SECONDS is 18.0 and _process silently decrements _prep_left until a wave starts on its own. The only mention is a 6-second message when the previous wave clears, so for the other 12 seconds the player has no idea how long they have to spend seeds and place plants. The threat tint now tells them how bad the next wave is and still nothing tells them when it lands.
acceptance_criteria: The HUD shows the remaining prep time and it visibly counts down; the readout disappears once a wave is live. Covered by a unit test that pumps _process and asserts the text changes.
close_reason: Closed

title: The message line has one slot, so cues stomp each other
description: Hud.show_message assigns _message_label.text outright and resets a single _message_left timer, so any new message destroys the one before it mid-read. The uproot gate made this concrete: the 4s 'click again to uproot' instruction is wiped by the 2s husk message the moment a pest dies, and the player is left with an armed button and no explanation. A short queue, or a second line, or at minimum refusing to overwrite a higher-priority message before it has been readable.
acceptance_criteria: A message cannot be replaced before a minimum readable time unless the new one is higher priority; the uproot instruction survives an incidental husk pickup. Unit test drives two overlapping show_message calls and asserts what the label reads.
close_reason: Closed

title: A real end-of-run summary panel
description: _end_run paints the run's whole damage map on the board and names the worst cell in a 30s message that expires while the player is still reading the banner. Every number a post-mortem needs is already computed -- waves survived, threat level reached, seeds earned, high score, worst lane cell, husks collected vs dropped. Give them a panel that stays until dismissed, instead of a banner plus a timed message.
acceptance_criteria: An end-of-run panel showing at least waves survived, threat level reached, seeds earned and the worst lane cell, which persists until the player restarts; covered by a headless UI test.
close_reason: RunSummary card with waves/threat/beds/compost/worst-cell, persists until dismissed, replay and back-to-title both wired and verified live

title: Show a selected plant's health in the side panel
description: Hungry pests chew plants down over several seconds and Plant.health drives a bar on the plant itself, but the selection panel shows only the name and blurb. Selecting a half-eaten Corn Cobbler tells the player nothing about whether to uproot and replant it, which is exactly the decision the panel exists to support. Add a health readout to the selection box.
acceptance_criteria: The selection panel shows current/max health for a damaged plant and updates as it takes damage; a unit test drives take_damage and asserts the panel text changed.
close_reason: Health bar + numbers in the selection panel, hidden until damaged, green->red ramp; runtime caught a zero-margin panel foot which is now fixed and gated at 8px

title: Uproot needs a confirm or an undo
description: The Uproot button refunds 60% and destroys the plant instantly with no confirmation. One stray click on a selected Sunflower late in a run silently destroys the economy the whole run was built on -- it is the only irreversible misclick in the game. Add a confirm step (the button re-labels to 'Uproot? Confirm' for a few seconds) or a short undo window that restores the plant and reverses the refund.
acceptance_criteria: A single click on Uproot does not remove the plant; a second within the window does. Unit tests cover both the confirm path and the timeout-cancels path.
close_reason: request_uproot() arms on first click, commits on a second within 4s; verified live (232x40 relabel, exact UPROOT_ARMED red, timeout revert) and covered by 4 tests

title: Designer's Notebook reads as two floating images, not a notebook
description: Six pages, each a bare 320x320 drawing beside a bare 320x320 sprite on a flat dark field, with one six-word green caption and three default buttons below. Nothing says which pane is which, the sprite renders blurry (64px source filtered up to 320), there is no keyboard paging or Escape, no transition between pages, and the page/sprite mapping is wrong in places (image6 is the named Corn Cobbler portrait, not the kernel volley; image3 is where the kernels are).
acceptance_criteria: A paper spread with a binding so it reads as a notebook; per-pane headings; crisp sprite rendering; a real designer note per page, not just a caption; correct drawing-to-sprite mapping; page dots; Left/Right arrows page and Escape closes; a cross-fade between pages; Drawing/Sprite/PageLabel/Backdrop stay direct children of the root so existing tests and bridge paths hold.
close_reason: Closed

title: Title screen is a flat rectangle with default-theme buttons
description: The title screen draws INK over the whole viewport, three stock grey Buttons and three Labels. No art, no motion, no keyboard, and the bottom third is empty — in a game that already ships plant and pest sprites. It is the first thing a player sees and it looks unfinished.
acceptance_criteria: A themed button set (paper/ink/leaf, hover + focus states); a drawn backdrop instead of one flat colour; the game's own sprites on screen; an entrance animation that is skipped headlessly; keyboard focus and Enter to start; existing node paths (Backdrop/StartButton/EndlessButton/NotebookButton) unchanged so tests and the bridge still resolve.
close_reason: Closed

title: HUD compost counter collides with the Grow-the-next-wave button
description: With several husks on the ground the HUD reads 'Compost 0 (11 ready)' and the '(11 ready)' suffix runs underneath the 'Grow the next wave' button. Caught in a screenshot during /verify on 2026-08-15; validate-ui reported 0 findings over that exact frame because the label's own rect is fine -- it is the button that overlaps it, and nothing compares two sibling Controls for occlusion. Give the HUD bar a real layout (HBoxContainer with the button in its own slot) so the counter cannot be run over regardless of how long its text gets.
acceptance_criteria: A HUD with a 2-digit husk count and the wave button both visible has no overlapping screen rects, asserted by node-bounds in a test.
close_reason: Closed

title: Mutated pests should drop a better husk
description: Armoured/winged/hungry mutations all cost the player more to deal with than a plain pest, but _on_pest_died pays the same husk value regardless of mutation. Scale husk value by mutation (e.g. armoured/winged/hungry each worth more) to tie the mutation system into the compost system instead of leaving them side by side.
close_reason: Pest.husk_multiplier() scales husk value by mutation (armoured/winged 1.5x, hungry 2x); verified headless (4 unit tests) and live (compost_state: plain=2, hungry=3)

title: Lane pressure readout on the road
description: The board is a single road, so which end pests got furthest on last wave is always answerable but never shown. Tint the road segment red where pests advanced furthest last wave, fading each wave, to give the player a passive read on lane pressure without opening any menu.
close_reason: LanePressureOverlay tints the road cell where pests got furthest last wave; verified headless (4 unit tests, one of which caught a real game-over-mid-wave commit bug) and live (board_info + run-method + screenshot)

title: Selection needs a second cue beyond the range ring
description: Right now the only sign a plant is selected is the translucent range ring — Corn Cobbler shows it, but Chomp Flower draws no ring at all, so selecting a Chomp shows nothing. Add a thin outline or corner brackets drawn on the sprite itself in the base Plant class (not per-subclass), so selection is legible for every current and future plant.
close_reason: SelectionMarker child node ships in Plant, verified headless (2 unit tests) and at runtime (get-state + screenshot)

title: Corn range indicator on selected plant
description: Placement is blind: corn reaches 176px and nothing shows it. Draw a range ring around the plant when selected/placing so the player can judge coverage.
close_reason: Wired Plant.set_selected() into Game._select() (closes G-007) and added ChompFlower's shrinking chew ring; both verified at runtime via /verify.

title: Chomp Flower occupied readout
description: chew_progress() exists on ChompFlower and nothing draws it. The Chomp/beetle trade-off (mouth busy ~2.6s, lane open) is invisible to the player. Draw a shrinking ring/bar around the flower while chewing.
close_reason: Wired Plant.set_selected() into Game._select() (closes G-007) and added ChompFlower's shrinking chew ring; both verified at runtime via /verify.

title: Sprite pass 2: damaged/eating/dead states
description: The design doc draws a Chomp mid-bite and an X-eyed pest; those are separate sprites, not tints.
close_reason: Implemented and /verify'd in the 2026-08-15 session: sprite pass 2 (eating/dead states), pest mutations from wave 8, tiered seed packets + Seed Sunflower (3rd plant), title screen + endless mode, and the Designer's Notebook screen. See log-devtools.md and kanban.md.

title: Pest waves: aphid swarms and beetle heavies
description: Aphid = fast/weak, Beetle = slow/tanky and survives a Chomp long enough to matter.
close_reason: Closed

title: Chomp Flower melee: instant on small pests, slow chew on big ones
description: 'eats small pests easily, takes a while eating bigger pests' — occupied-while-chewing is the whole balance lever.
close_reason: Closed

title: Corn Cobbler firing: single kernel, then the 'bunch of corn' burst
description: Design doc shows a single projectile upgrading to a spread of kernels.
close_reason: Closed

title: Seed economy: earn seeds, buy seed packets to unlock plants
description: 'You have to buy plant seeds to get plants' — seed drops from killed pests, a packet shop, and a run-persistent unlock set.
close_reason: Closed

title: Plant placement and the one free starter plant
description: Corn Cobbler is free at wave 1 per the design doc; every other plant costs seeds.
close_reason: Closed

title: Grid + path playfield from the Kenney tilesheet
description: Build the top-down lane using assets/kenney/png terrain tiles: dirt path over grass, buildable plots, spawn and base tiles.
close_reason: Closed

title: Read the design brief's combat claims against the coverage system
description:
SOURCE: the design brief. DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THIS CYCLE'S NEIGHBOURHOOD in subject, though it touches the same system -- cycle 55 was UI cues, this is the document.

Five cycles have now produced measurements the brief predates: coverage is not engagement (a cob fires at one pest), a minimal cover loses pests a redundant one stops, dead ground differs per plant and moved in opposite directions when the road changed, and the road's paint is out of channels.

If the brief describes coverage as a solved or simple idea, it is now describing something the game does not do. Audit just its combat and coverage claims -- not the whole document, which is -hwo6's larger job -- and cite file:line for anything marked shipped, per kanban-staleness-audit's bar.

ACCEPTANCE: a per-claim verdict for the brief's combat section.

title: Teach kanban-staleness-audit the derive-vs-record question
description:
SOURCE: this cycle's step 5 reflection.

Cycle 54 set out to derive five recorded road figures and correctly derived only two. The deciding question was derive-the-list's: is the membership a RULE or a TASTE CALL? The walled mouth list is a rule ('one beside every road cell'). Seven cobs is a taste call ('enough firepower'), and deriving it produced a better cover, a weaker garden, and two broken tests.

That question generalises past lists to the whole backlog: a kanban entry proposing to 'automate' or 'derive' something needs it asked BEFORE the work, not after. It is the cheapest possible staleness check and it is not in the audit skill.

ACCEPTANCE: kanban-staleness-audit names the rule-vs-taste-call question and cites cycle 54 as the case where deriving was measurably the wrong call.

title: Surface dead ground before the player is holding a plant
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (54)', third entry. PLAYER-FACING.

The dead-ground cue is per-plant and appears at placement time. So a player scanning the board to decide WHAT to buy sees uniform grass, and only learns a corner is useless after committing to a plant.

Cycle 53 sharpened this: the reshape moved Corn dead ground 15 -> 11 and Chomp 34 -> 36, in OPPOSITE directions. A player who learned 'the top-right is useless' on one board has learned something false about the next.

Overlaps -g8kc (tint ground no plant can use), which is the always-true subset. This one is the harder, more useful version: show the currently-SELECTED plant's dead ground on hover over the shop entry, before purchase.

ACCEPTANCE: hovering a shop entry previews that plant's dead ground on the board; a test asserts the preview matches PlacementPreview's own answer for that plant.

title: Show a par score for garden efficiency on the run summary
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (54)', second entry. PLAYER-FACING.

test_combat.gd's _cover_greedily now computes the SMALLEST garden reaching every road cell -- five cobs on the current road. That number is a genuinely interesting thing to know and it already computes.

The player currently gets no signal about whether their garden was efficient or merely large. game/run_summary.gd is where a par would land: 'you held the road with 11 plants; 5 would have reached it'. It reframes a won run as a puzzle with a better answer, which is the cheapest replay motivation available.

Careful: reaching every cell is NOT the same as holding the road -- that is exactly what cycle 54 found, since the minimal cover loses pests the redundant one stops. So the par must be described as REACH, not as a garden that would have won, or it teaches something false.

ACCEPTANCE: the summary shows a reach-par; its wording distinguishes reach from sufficiency; a test asserts the par against a known road.
notes: Cycle 55 strengthens the case: test_combat's _cover_greedily now computes the minimal garden reaching every road cell, so the par number is already written and tested rather than needing to be invented. -f909 was filed as a duplicate note and closed.

title: Tint ground no plant in the catalogue can use
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (53)', third entry. PLAYER-FACING.

The reshape opened bigger clearings: the Chomp's 74 px grab radius now strands 36 of 94 buildable cells, up from 34, while the Corn's 176 px ring strands only 11. The dead-ground cue is per-plant and appears at placement time, so a player scanning the board before choosing a plant sees uniform grass.

Ground that NO plant in the catalogue can use is different in kind -- it is scenery, permanently -- and a faint permanent tint would say so without teaching anything false about the per-plant cue. The count is small: cells dead for the LONGEST reach in the catalogue.

Careful: this number changes when a plant with a longer reach is unlocked or added, so it must be derived from PlantCatalog rather than recorded, and it should probably consider only plants the player has actually unlocked.

ACCEPTANCE: the tint is derived from the catalogue's maximum reach, updates when a plant unlocks, and is asserted by a test that adds a longer-reach plant and watches it shrink.

title: Show when a covered cell is covered by a plant that is already busy
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (53)', second entry. PLAYER-FACING.

Six cobs reach all 32 road cells and a pest still crossed unfought, because _furthest_along_in_range (game/corn_cobbler.gd:109) picks exactly ONE target. The board's coverage cue tells a player a cell is covered; it cannot tell them the plant covering it is permanently committed elsewhere.

That gap is measured already -- the over-promise tests count 'unanswered' stays on covered ground and the figure is large (65% in one recorded run). So the data exists and only the cue is missing.

Design care needed: this must not read as 'the cell is uncovered', which is false, and it must not fire constantly during a heavy wave, which would make it noise. A second tint or a hatch on covered-but-contested ground, shown only while a wave runs.

ACCEPTANCE: a player can tell 'covered' from 'covered and contested' at a glance, and a test drives a wave and asserts the cue appears on the cells the over-promise run identifies.

title: Audit the design brief against what the game actually does
description:
SOURCE: step 0's third pre-flight item plus the design brief. DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THIS CYCLE'S NEIGHBOURHOOD -- cycle 52 was entirely the HUD message row and tooling.

scope-vs-claim's four shapes are all about a CHECK describing itself. The same asymmetry applies to a design document: it states what the game is, nothing compares that to what the game does, and the prose is what a reader trusts.

The brief has never been audited. Cycles 49-52 have found that a user-requested feature already shipped (facing direction), that kanban's Done section has never been read back, and that a standing note in cycle-log.md was wrong about a number -- all the same shape. The brief is the largest unaudited claim surface left.

Use kanban-staleness-audit's bar: before writing that something is missing, open the code that would contain it. Expect a third of it to be shipped, a third stale, a third still real -- and the value is in knowing which.

ACCEPTANCE: a per-claim verdict with file:line for anything marked shipped.

title: Gather the message-corpus waiver reasons into one place
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (52)', third entry.

The five `# message-corpus-check: ok - <reason>` waivers (game/game.gd:231, :1397, :1464, :1468, :1605) are collectively the best documentation of what the message row can show that cannot be priced statically. Each says something true and non-obvious.

But the answer to 'what can the row show that we cannot measure?' is now assembled by grep -- which is EXACTLY the failure the corpus just fixed one level down, reappearing in the waivers that made the fix possible.

Cheapest fix: have message_corpus_check print the waived sites AND their reasons on a clean run, not just the count. The information is already parsed; it is one line per waiver, and it turns a grep into an output.

ACCEPTANCE: a clean run names each waived site and its reason.

title: Derive message durations from length instead of picking six numbers
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (52)', second entry. PLAYER-FACING.

show_message() durations are hand-picked and unrelated: 8.0s opening hint (game/game.gd:264), 6.0s wave cleared (:415), 4.0s eaten (:1197), 5.0s packet (:1407), 2.5s mute and colourblind (:1464, :1484), 2.0s uproot cancelled and husk swept (:1319, :1588).

The spread is probably RIGHT -- a message you must read to act on should outlast a confirmation -- but nothing states the rule, so the next message added gets a number by vibes. Reading time scales with length, and Hud.message_corpus() now knows every length.

A duration derived from character count with a floor and a ceiling would make 8.0 and 2.0 consequences of one decision rather than eight independent ones. Keep an explicit override for anything that genuinely needs to outlast its length.

ACCEPTANCE: durations come from one function; every current value is either reproduced by it or carries a written reason for its override.

title: Audit STYLE.md's claims against the art the way the budgets were audited
description:
SOURCE: step 0's third pre-flight item, applying scope-vs-claim. DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THIS CYCLE'S NEIGHBOURHOOD -- cycle 51 was budgets, tests and skills.

art_src/STYLE.md states conventions the art is supposed to obey; line 14 says facing is up-screen (-Y) for anything directional. Cycle 50 checked that claim against the three pest SVGs by hand and it held. Nobody has checked its OTHER claims against the other sixteen SVGs.

This is scope-vs-claim shape 1 at repo scale: a document states a scope ('anything directional') and nothing compares it to what exists. svg_style_check.py already parses the art for palette conformance, so there is a place to put whatever turns out to be mechanically checkable.

ACCEPTANCE: a per-claim verdict for STYLE.md; anything checkable moved into svg_style_check.py with a fixture, anything not checkable narrowed in the prose so it stops implying a guarantee.
notes: Third piece of evidence (cycle 56): two new drawn cues shipped in cycles 55 and 56 -- PlacementPreview's new-cover dots and SoleCoverMarks' sole-cover rings -- and neither was checked against STYLE.md's conventions. -6v8n was filed as a duplicate note and closed.

title: Check whether the wave-cleared line eats the prep note's window
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (51)', third entry. PLAYER-FACING.

_paint_message_row gives a transient message precedence over the standing note (established in cycle 48, and correct). wave_cleared_line (game/hud.gd:1655) fires exactly when the prep note becomes relevant: at the end of a wave, when the player is deciding what to plant next.

So the question is whether the cleared line's duration overlaps the window in which someone reads the forecast. If it does, the player is told what just happened during the seconds they need to be told what is coming.

This is a design question and the precedence is deliberate -- do not 'fix' it by inverting the rule. Measure the overlap first: use pause + _message_left, per .claude/skills/read-a-moving-value.

ACCEPTANCE: a measured verdict on the overlap, and a decision recorded either way.

title: Kill pests differently depending on what killed them
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (50)', third entry. PLAYER-FACING JUICE, which this cycle and the two before it produced almost none of.

test_a_pest_killed_mid_stride_leaves_a_straight_corpse asserts a corpse lies on its facing with the gait lean undone -- a genuinely nice touch that already ships, and the hook is already there in Pest.kill(). Right now a Chomp bite, a Corn Cobbler kernel and a seed bomb all produce the same straight corpse.

Differentiating them is cheap on a system that already has the seam: a bite could leave a shorter corpse or a bitten-off angle, a kernel a knockback along its travel, a bomb a scatter. Keep the existing straight-corpse assertion true for at least one path so the test does not have to be rewritten wholesale.

ACCEPTANCE: at least two death sources produce visibly different corpses, each asserted.

title: Gate the weather multipliers with assert_margin too
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (50)', second entry.

-frzz covers the pest gait constants. The weather multipliers have exactly the same shape and no bead: WEATHER_DROUGHT_SEED_BONUS (1.5) and WEATHER_RAIN_HEAL_FRACTION in game/wave_director.gd, both tuned, both with reasoning in prose, neither asserted against the corpus of values sitting near them.

_T.assert_margin(values, threshold, margin, recorded) exists for precisely this. A tuned constant with a documented justification and no test is a comment, not a contract -- and cycle 48 showed what that costs when the corpus a measurement claims drifts from the one it sweeps.

ACCEPTANCE: a test that fails if a weather multiplier moves close enough to 1.0 that the weather stops being distinguishable, or close enough to another weather's value that the two stop being different choices.

title: Add a level whose road climbs, exercising the -Y facing branch
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md 'New this cycle (50)', first entry, which came out of the runtime pass on -ymth.

Board._build_route() (game/board.gd:162) walks _path_order, and the shipped level's route -- read live off a pest, thirty-four points -- runs right, down, left, down, right. Not one -Y step. So Pest._update_facing()'s `_facing = 0.0` branch (game/pest.gd:679) has never executed in a real game.

A road that CLIMBS is the cheapest new-level variety available: the art already exists and rests up-screen, the code path already works and is now asserted (test_update_facing_maps_every_cardinal_to_the_art_up_screen_convention), and it makes the vertical axis mean something in both directions rather than only downward.

ACCEPTANCE: a level whose _path_order contains at least one upward step, and a pest observed on it rendering with rotation 0.
close_reason: Road reshaped to (0,1)-(6,1)-(6,4)-(2,4)-(2,7)-(9,7)-(9,3)-(13,3): climbs up column 9, holds 32 cells / 2112 px so no length-derived constant moved. Five shape-dependent tests re-derived. Confirmed on screen at _facing=0.0. dc3820f

title: Build screen-content-audit, or record why not
description:
SOURCE: step 0's second pre-flight item (skill ideas in log.md vs .claude/skills/).

log.md:3267 names it: 'given a screen and its content table, check that every entry resolves to a DISTINCT asset (by content hash, not path), that every text field is non-empty and within the box it is given, and that no two entries claim the same source.' Three defects in one session were that check at different angles -- a duplicate photograph, an ellipsised note, a kernel stretched from 32px to 190px -- and all three shipped in a table that read as entirely correct.

ONE identification so far, so this is not yet at step 0's build-it bar. Filed to make the second identification land against something instead of being written down again. Cycle 45 established the good precedent here: decide NOT to build a checker when precision would be low, and record the measurement that says so. Either build it or write that measurement.

ACCEPTANCE: the skill exists, or a written count of how many real findings it would have produced against the screens this game actually has.

title: Gate the pest gait constants with assert_margin
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md, 'New this cycle (49)', third entry.

GAIT_SWING 0.13, GAIT_RATE 8.5, GAIT_REFERENCE_SPEED 60.0, GAIT_RATE_MIN 0.55, GAIT_RATE_MAX 1.9 (game/pest.gd:235-245). The header gives real reasoning for the reference speed -- between the aphid's 78 and the beetle's 38, so the fast one scuttles and the slow one plods without a per-species constant -- and nothing asserts it.

That reasoning is exactly what _T.assert_margin(values, threshold, margin, recorded) gates: it checks the corpus items sitting near a tuned value. A species added at speed 61 would land on the boundary silently today.

ACCEPTANCE: a test that fails when a species' speed is close enough to GAIT_REFERENCE_SPEED that the constant's stated justification no longer holds.

title: Audit the six oldest kanban sections against the code they claim about
description:
SOURCE: step 0's third backlog (kanban.md), which says at its own top that the historical sections are unpruned and roughly half stale.

DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THIS CYCLE'S NEIGHBOURHOOD (the cycle-34 rule): everything else filed this cycle touches budgets, weather or the HUD message row. This one touches none of them.

The kanban-staleness-audit skill exists (.claude/skills/kanban-staleness-audit/) and has never been run over the historical sections -- it was built in cycle 34 after being named as missing three times, and then applied only to STILL REAL. Run it over the six oldest 'New this cycle' sections. The cycle-31 rule requires a file:line for every claim about current code; entries predating that rule have none, which is exactly what makes them unfalsifiable and why they rot.

ACCEPTANCE: each audited entry is either deleted, moved to Done with the commit that did it, or given the file:line that makes it checkable.

title: Cap the wave number's width in next_wave_note, or say the budget bounds it
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md, 'New this cycle (48)', third entry.

_budget_hud_message_row now measures Hud.next_wave_note(999, 9999, ...) (game/game.gd:2071) deliberately -- a budget is about what the FORMAT allows, not what the game is expected to reach. But next_wave_note (game/hud.gd:1505) formats the wave number with no width cap, so the budget's worst case is set by a digit count nothing in the code constrains. Endless mode has no wave ceiling, so 999 is a guess wearing a worst-case's clothes.

Either cap the formatted number (and assert the cap), or write in next_wave_note's own header that its width is bounded by the budget's chosen maximum and not by the format -- so the next person to widen it knows where the real limit lives.

ACCEPTANCE: a test that fails if the note can exceed the width the budget assumes.

title: Decide what rain pays, now that drought pays 150%
description:
SOURCE: kanban.md, 'New this cycle (48)', first entry -- direct consequence of closing -4c1l.

WaveDirector.seed_multiplier_for returns 1.5 for drought and 1.0 for everything else. Rain still heals pests (WEATHER_RAIN_HEAL_FRACTION) and pays base rate, so it is now the only weather with a downside and no compensation. A forecast the player reads has one weather they want and two they don't, which is a worse decision space than before the bonus existed.

Three shapes: rain pays a smaller bonus; rain gets a non-seed upside (faster regrowth, a free replant); or drought's bonus shrinks and rain's heal shrinks with it. NOTE the overlap with -oo7e (weather has no counter-play, blocked on the user): if weather gains a real counter, this rebalance is downstream of that decision and should not be done first.

ACCEPTANCE: every weather has at least one thing the player wants about it, named in next_wave_note before the wave commits.

title: Check that comments citing a verb or a test are still true
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (29 of 30)'. Measured this cycle: five comments in game/ name a devtools verb and ONE named a verb that does not exist (both commit_uproot headers claimed 'the devtools verbs' call it; list-commands --offline has nothing matching uproot). Nine comments name a test_* function, eight of which exist -- the ninth is test_selftest, a FILE name, which any checker must accept. Both classes are cheap to verify: list-commands --offline parses registrations with no game running, and test functions are a grep of test/. Build them as ONE 'comments that cite something' pass rather than two thin checkers; high precision, low volume, and this project leans hard on 'the alarm is test_X' as documentation.

title: Name every node the code keeps a reference to
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (28 of 30)'. 123 add_child calls in game/ against 93 .name assignments. The selection marker was in that gap: drawn on every selected plant, path @SelectionMarker@31, addressable from no test and no bridge command -- in a project whose OverlayScreen header says node paths are a contract. Not every anonymous node is a defect, but nothing distinguishes deliberate from overlooked. Derivable rule for a checker: a node that is add_child-ed AND stored in a member variable is one the code will refer to again, so a test or the bridge probably wants to as well.

title: Count hosted nodes that did not survive the test
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (27 of 30)'. _T.free_ui(host) runs at the end of every hosting test and a node that freed ITSELF in between is indistinguishable from one that did not. Counting what was hosted against what survives would have surfaced this cycle's defect as a warning on its first run, years of cycles earlier. Same caveat as the sibling bead: run_tests.gd is harness-owned, so this is an upstream proposal, but the measurement can be prototyped locally in a test first.

title: Refuse an equality assertion whose two sides are the same object

description: Zero create_tween calls in hud.gd, while plant.gd, corn_cobbler.gd, chomp_flower.gd, sunflower.gd, pest.gd, title_screen.gd and notebook_screen.gd all animate. title: The common packet button stays lit once its tier is exhausted
description: Hud disables the common packet button only on locked_empty or seeds < cost. title: A Corn Cobbler at full bunch looks exactly like a fresh one
description: CornCobbler.LEVELS takes kernels 1 to 2 to 5 and spread_degrees 0 to 14 to 52, and upgrade() only bumps the level integer. Plant loads one texture once and never changes it, and RANGE is flat at every level. So the single most expensive decision in the game -- paying seeds to upgrade -- produces no visible change on the board at all. The only readout is a line in the selection panel, which requires clicking the plant to see.

title: Project-identity devtools verb so a session can prove which build it is driving
description: A sibling git worktree of this project had its own Godot running and answered this session's devtools bus, because user:// is keyed on project name and shared across worktrees. It cost most of one runtime pass: symptoms were 'no Game in the tree' and node-not-found on paths that plainly existed, which reads as your own scene being broken. Register a project verb returning ProjectSettings.globalize_path('res://') plus the git branch, so any session can assert in one call that it is talking to its own build. Upstream fix filed as G-018; this is the local guard.
acceptance_criteria: cmd project_identity returns the absolute res:// path; a documented one-liner in CLAUDE.md compares it against the working directory before a runtime pass.
close_reason: project_identity verb reports project_root, user_dir, git branch/sha read from disk, worktree-aware; verified live against git rev-parse and offline discovery

title: Tint the threat level as it climbs
description: threat_level() renders as a small integer in the same cream as every other readout, so 'this wave is worse than the last' is something the player has to read and compare rather than see. Tint the threat portion of the wave label green -> amber -> red across the level range so the escalation is preattentive. The level is already a pure static function, so this is a colour lookup.
acceptance_criteria: A static Hud.threat_colour(level) with tests pinning the endpoints and monotonic movement between them; the label uses it.

title: Placement preview should warn when a non-combat plant is road-adjacent
description: A hungry pest eats whatever plant is nearest and a Sunflower cannot fight back, but nothing on screen says 'this tile is one hungry mutation away from losing your economy plant'. PlacementPreview already computes reach and legality per cell, so this is nearly free now: road-adjacency is one is_path check on the four neighbours, and the preview is the node that would draw the warning. Only applies to plants with PlantCatalog.reach(id) == 0.0 -- a Corn Cobbler next to the road is fine, that is the point of it.
acceptance_criteria: Hovering a grass cell orthogonally adjacent to the road with the Sunflower selected draws a distinct warning cue; the same cell with a Corn Cobbler selected does not; both covered by unit tests.
close_reason: Closed

title: Per-run lane pressure for the end-of-run post-mortem

It cannot answer 'which cell has bled me all game'. Accumulate a second, never-faded tally alongside the per-wave one and show it on the end-of-run screen, so the post-mortem tells the player where their garden was actually weak.
acceptance_criteria: Board keeps a run-total pressure map separate from the decaying per-wave one; the end-of-run banner or screen renders it; a unit test shows the run map surviving fades that clear the wave map.

title: Show a readable threat level for endless mode

Derive one threat number (or a wave-start banner naming what went up this wave) from the five WaveDirector static functions, which are already pure and callable without a running wave. This is a readout, not a new system.

title: A richer husk should rot faster, so sweep order becomes a decision
description: Husk size and glow now scale with value, but the timer does not: a 9-seed husk and a 2-seed one both rot in exactly CompostMeter.HUSK_LIFETIME (10s). Sweeping in any order is therefore optimal and the board asks nothing. Scale the lifetime inversely with value (a richer husk decays faster) so 'which one first?' is a real decision, and so the new size cue carries urgency as well as worth.
acceptance_criteria: drop_husk stores a per-husk lifetime derived from value; HuskLayer's rot ring reads that instead of the constant; a unit test shows a high-value husk expiring before a low-value one dropped at the same moment.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lane pressure should record every cell pests were lost at, not just the worst
description: Board.record_lane_pressure only ever receives the single furthest-reached cell for a wave (Game._wave_worst_cell), so a wave where pests died at scattered points along the lane only ever lights up the worst one. Recording every cell a pest died/escaped at (not just the max) would draw the whole 'where the damage happened' picture instead of one hot pixel.
close_reason: Closed

title: Endless mode should scale pest health/speed too
description: WaveDirector._endless_groups scales count/gap and mutation_chance_for scales mutation chance as endless mode runs longer, but Pest.SPECIES health/speed stay fixed forever -- a wave-60 pest is exactly as tough as a wave-9 one. Scale health and/or speed slightly past some endless threshold, mirroring the mutation-chance climb, so late-game pressure isn't pure quantity.

title: Husk size/glow should scale with value
description: HuskLayer._draw() draws every husk at a fixed 9px radius regardless of CompostMeter's stored value, so a mutated pest's 1.5-2x husk_multiplier() payout is invisible until clicked. Scale the drawn radius (or ring brightness) by value so a bigger payout reads visually across the board, the way mutation tints already do for the pest itself.

title: Second bite frame for a beetle's long chew
description: chomp_flower_eating.png is one fixed picture for the whole chew animation, aphid or beetle alike, even though a beetle's chew is 2.6s — long enough to read a second frame. Swap in an 'almost done' frame once chew_progress() > 0.6 (the same threshold the shrinking ring already reads) to sell 'big pests take a while' with just a second sprite and one if-check.
close_reason: chomp_flower_eating_late.png swaps in past chew_progress()>0.6 (LATE_BITE_THRESHOLD); verified headless (3 ChompFlower unit tests + sprite style contract) and live (texture path polled across a real slow-motion beetle chew, crossing exactly at 61%)

title: Say in CLAUDE.md that list-commands has an offline mode
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (29 of 30)'. The verb table describes list-commands as runtime discovery for a launched session. Its --offline mode parses the registration sites statically with no game at all, which makes 'does a verb by this name exist' a free question -- that is what disproved a stale doc claim this cycle in one command. The harness section is regenerated by scaffold, so this note belongs in the project's own part of CLAUDE.md rather than inside the managed block.

title: Write down what 'armed' looks like, once
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (28 of 30)'. Two surfaces now show a pending destructive change and they use different second channels: a bullet mark on the Keys screen's rows, doubled line weight on the board's selection marker. Both are correct for their surface -- a Label and a draw_line shape have different vocabularies -- and together they mean the project has no single answer to 'what does armed look like', which is the kind of thing that drifts as surfaces are added. Write the pair down beside GardenTheme.DANGER so the third surface inherits a decision rather than inventing one.

title: Give Pest a last_survivable_leg() instead of re-deriving it by eye
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (27 of 30)'. Three test files build pests with hand-set _leg values against hand-written routes, and the relationship between 'a route of N points' and 'the last leg a pest can sit on without escaping' is _route.size() - 2, written down nowhere and re-derived by eye each time. Getting it wrong by one is exactly this cycle's bug. Either expose it on Pest or give the tests a helper that places a pest at a FRACTION of its route, so no test does the arithmetic.

title: Make verify_ledger stats show the suite count over time
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (26 of 30)'. The bisect that proved gh#43 rested on a suite count taken by hand before the install. .devtools/verify-runs.jsonl already records tests.total per run, so the history exists -- a stats line reading '552 for the last 12 runs, 0 this run' would surface a dependency regression without anyone remembering to take a before-measurement. Cheap, and it turns the ledger from a record into an alarm.

title: Check that every glyph the game draws exists in the font
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (24 of 30)'. A missing glyph renders as a .notdef box with a real width, so GardenTheme.measure() returns a plausible number, every width budget passes, and the only way this project has ever caught one is by looking at a screenshot. Font.has_char() exists. Worth pairing with the glyph table above: once every glyph is named in one place, asserting the font has all of them is a loop.

title: Mark which budget floors have actually been tested
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (23 of 30)'. hud_readouts (10px) and hud_stats_row (19px) earned their floors by being pushed through them in anger. hud_message_row's 40px is a number picked while declaring it, with 342px of headroom, and cmd budgets reports the two kinds identically -- so a floor that has never been approached looks exactly like one that has been defended. Either add a field saying so, or say it in the constant's comment; the goal is that a reader can tell a measured floor from a placeholder.

title: Say how much game is left, not just what is next
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (22 of 30)'. The last-wave note is the only place the game admits a run is nearly over. The prep strip, the wave counter and the threat number all describe the NEXT wave without ever saying how much is left. WaveDirector.WAVES.size() is static and current_wave is on every state dict, so '3 waves to go' is available everywhere and used nowhere. Endless has no answer, which is itself the interesting design question rather than a blocker.

title: Decide how a FIRST record is celebrated
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (20 of 30)'. The roll deliberately refuses when previous_best is 0: counting up from a zero the player never held is a lie. But a first-ever record is the most significant one they will set and currently gets LESS than a later, smaller one, which is backwards. The answer is a different treatment rather than a roll -- decide what, then build it. Filed as a decision, not as work.

title: Roll the seeds counter the way the record rolls
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (20 of 30)'. The seeds readout moves far more often than the record does. Hud._punch_readout already scales it on change, so 'this number moved' machinery exists and stops short of showing the movement -- a 45-seed purchase reads as a jump. Use the pattern from TitleScreen._arm_record_ratchet: a pure renderer, the final text set first, a restoring callback. Note the difference: seeds go DOWN as well as up, and a roll downward needs deciding rather than assuming.

title: Give kanban.md entries ids so their status can be derived too
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (19 of 30)'. kanban.md has the same shape log-devtools.md had: an entry's real status is whichever mention is newest, and cycles 34 and 36 each found a section whose heading said 'not filed yet' over entries that had shipped. A kanban_ledger sibling to gap_ledger.py is the obvious tool and cannot be written, because kanban entries have no ids to key on. The enabling change is small -- a [K-NNN] on each entry under the idea backlog -- and it is the prerequisite, not the tool.

title: Decide whether a drought should slow the non-shooters
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (18 of 30)'. Plant.fire_interval_scale is read by CornCobbler and Dandelion only; Chomp, Sundew and Sunflower pace themselves by other means (is_busy(), droplets, a growth gauge), so a drought slows two plants of five. That is arguably right -- a drought should hurt shooting, not chewing -- but it is an accident of which plants happen to read the multiplier rather than a decision anyone wrote down. Decide it, then either write the reasoning into Plant.fire_interval_scale's doc comment or extend it.

title: Pay more for surviving a wave under weather
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (17 of 30)'. SeedBank does not know weather exists, so surviving the hardest version of a wave pays exactly what the easy version pays. WaveDirector.threat_for() already exists and already rises monotonically -- it is the natural place to hang a payout multiplier, and doing it there rather than in SeedBank keeps 'how hard was that' in the one file that already answers it.
close_reason: Drought pays 150% on direct seed drops (WEATHER_DROUGHT_SEED_BONUS), named in next_wave_note and weather_note. Also corrected _budget_hud_message_row, which measured only plant names and not the prep note now widest on that row. bce07e5

title: Align the key column across the two screens that show keys
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (16 of 30)'. The pause card now right-aligns its keys against a gutter (game/pause_screen.gd:_build_key_list); KeyBindingScreen centres its RowKey%d labels in a fixed 140px column (game/key_binding_screen.gd:85), neither derived nor matching. Two screens showing the same eight keys in two different alignments is the kind of thing nobody reports and everybody notices. Do it after the shared measurement lands.

title: Widen the mirror gate to the other prose invariants
description: Source: cycle 32's step 5 reflection. tools/mirror_check.py compares ONE named block in TWO named files, and says so under NOT COVERED. The repo has other prose that must agree with something: the parallel-safe gate list in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md must name every tools/*_check.py that exists (it is hand-maintained and a new checker can be forgotten -- three were added in three cycles), and the harness section's verb table must not name a verb list-commands does not report. Both are derivable rather than hand-checkable, which is the derive-the-list shape. Low priority: no instance of either drifting yet, unlike the mirror, which had two.

title: Show the key hint on the HUD's own buttons
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (15 of 30)'. The HUD's 'Grow the next wave' button has a keyboard verb behind it and never says so -- a player who rebinds a key sees it only on the two screens that own bindings. Drawing the hint from KeyBindings.label_for() makes a rebinding visible where the player actually is. Depends on the legend column split: this would be the third surface to show key names, and the pause card just spent a cycle learning that a key name a player chose can be far wider than one we shipped.

title: Widen SHORT_NAMES to the keys the engine names badly
description: Source: kanban.md 'New this cycle (14 of 30)'. KeyBindings.SHORT_NAMES (game/key_bindings.gd:121) covers 8 of the ~100 bindable keys -- Esc, four arrows, Space, two Enters. Everything else falls through to the engine's own name, fine for F1 and poor for punctuation (KEY_BRACKETLEFT renders as something no player calls it). Do it with the derive-the-list recipe rather than one complaint at a time: derive the set the engine names badly, assert SHORT_NAMES covers exactly it, plant both directions.
